text: And so I came in swinging ready to go, and then about a month into my time there, I got a meeting on my calendar.
speaker: Katie Dill
context: Lenny asks Katie about a significant failure in her leadership career. Katie describes her first month as head of design at Airbnb, where she tried to make rapid changes to improve the team's low engagement scores and collaboration issues. However, five team members scheduled a formal meeting with HR to read from papers listing everything they thought she was doing wrong as a leader.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 시작부터 의욕적으로 뛰어들었어요. 그런데 그곳에서 일한 지 한 달쯤 됐을 때 제 캘린더에 회의가 잡혔어요.
text_zh: 所以我一进公司就干劲十足准备大干一场，结果干了差不多一个月，我收到了一个会议邀请。
text_es: Y entonces llegué con todas las ganas, listo para arrancar, y como al mes de estar ahí, me aparece una reunión en el calendario.
key_sentence: I came in swinging ready to go
original_text: And so I came in swinging ready to go, and then about a month into my time there, I got a meeting on my calendar. Thursday 8:30 AM, was an hour and a half with half of the design team, so that was five people, and our HR partner. And so it was an extremely valuable learning experience and I took from that to then immediately shift how I was operating.

text: And regardless of each individual thing, what was very clear was that the missing piece, the theme that was across all of that is that I hadn't earned their trust.
speaker: Katie Dill
context: Katie explains her realization after receiving harsh feedback from her design team at Airbnb. The team had formally complained about her leadership approach through HR after just one month. Katie reflects on what she learned from this difficult experience about the importance of building trust as a foundation for effective leadership.
text_ko: 각각의 사안을 떠나서, 분명한 건 모든 경우에 공통된 한 가지는 제가 그들의 신뢰를 얻지 못했다는 점이었어요.
text_zh: 不管具体是哪件事，有一点很明确，就是所有这些问题的根源都指向一个问题——我还没有赢得他们的信任。
text_es: Y más allá de cada cosa en particular, lo que quedó clarísimo es que lo que faltaba, el hilo conductor de todo eso, era que no me había ganado su confianza.
key_sentence: the missing piece, the theme that was across all of that is that I hadn't earned their trust.
original_text: And regardless of each individual thing, what was very clear was that the missing piece, the theme that was across all of that is that I hadn't earned their trust. So whether how right or how wrong what I was doing was is the key piece is that I wasn't bringing the team along with me.

vocabulary.definition: An essential element or factor that is absent and necessary for achieving a complete understanding or successful outcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: Identifying the missing piece in a project or strategy can lead to breakthroughs in problem-solving and innovation within a business context.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often conveys a sense of incompleteness or urgency, implying that addressing the missing piece is critical for success.

text: I had some version of a panic attack, walked off stage, I was still mic'd up, cursed. I was laughing. I was like, 'Geez, are they laughing at me.
speaker: Paul Adams
context: Lenny asks Paul about a memorable failure that scarred him for life. Paul describes freezing during a keynote speech at the world's biggest advertising festival in Cannes, representing Facebook. He had to walk off stage in front of thousands of people, and because his microphone was still on, the audience heard him curse. Despite this nightmare scenario, he managed to return and successfully complete his presentation.
text_ko: 어떤 식으론 공황발작 비슷한 게 왔어요. 무대에서 내려왔는데도 마이크가 아직 붙어 있어서 욕이 나왔어요. 웃음도 나왔고, '아이구, 사람들이 나 보고 웃는 걸까?'라고 생각했어요.
text_zh: 我当时差点panic attack，直接走下台了，麦克风还开着呢，嘴里骂骂咧咧的。我还在那儿笑，心想"天哪，他们是在笑我吗？"
text_es: Tuve algo así como un ataque de pánico, me bajé del escenario, todavía tenía el micrófono puesto, dije groserías. Me estaba riendo. Y pensé, 'Dios mío, ¿se están burlando de mí?'
key_sentence: I was like, 'Geez, are they laughing at me.
original_text: I had some version of a panic attack, walked off stage, I was still mic'd up, cursed. I was laughing. I was like, 'Geez, are they laughing at me. Oh my God, this is...' But I can manage to turn it around, I walked back out, I'd kind of been disarmed internally in my head, and the rest of it went well.

vocabulary.definition: A sudden episode of intense fear or anxiety that triggers severe physical reactions when there is no real danger or apparent cause.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, a panic attack may occur during high-pressure situations such as public speaking or critical meetings, impacting an individual's performance and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with mental health issues, the term can also imply a loss of control in stressful situations, making it important to use with sensitivity.

text: I think a lot of the motivation for those projects came from a place of fear. It didn't come from a place of let's make a great product for people, let's really understand the things people struggle with when communicating with family and friends.
speaker: Paul Adams
context: Lenny asks Paul about his time working on failed social projects at Google like Google Buzz and Google+. Paul reflects on why these products failed, explaining that the motivation behind building them was fundamentally flawed. Instead of focusing on solving real user problems, the projects were driven by competitive fear of Facebook's success in social networking.
text_ko: 제 생각에 그 프로젝트들에 대한 동기 대부분은 두려움에서 나온 것 같아요. 사람들이 진짜로 필요로 하는 좋은 제품을 만들자거나, 가족·친구와 소통할 때 사람들이 어떤 어려움을 겪는지 제대로 이해해 보자는 마음에서 나온 건 아니었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得那些项目很多都是出于恐惧心理在做。不是真的想着怎么给用户做个好产品，怎么真正去了解大家跟家人朋友交流时会遇到什么困难。
text_es: Creo que gran parte de la motivación de esos proyectos venía del miedo. No venía de un lugar de "vamos a crear un producto genial para la gente", de realmente entender con qué luchan las personas cuando se comunican con familia y amigos.
key_sentence: a lot of the motivation for those projects came from a place of fear.
original_text: I think a lot of the motivation for those projects came from a place of fear. It didn't come from a place of let's make a great product for people, let's really understand the things people struggle with when communicating with family and friends. That's really, really try and create something wonderful. It came from a place of fear.

vocabulary.definition: The reason or reasons one has for acting or behaving in a particular way; the driving force behind actions and decisions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, motivation often refers to the underlying factors that inspire teams to pursue projects, innovate, and achieve goals, which can significantly impact productivity and company culture.
vocabulary.nuance: While motivation can stem from positive incentives, it can also arise from fear or pressure, which may lead to short-term results but potentially harm long-term engagement.

vocabulary.definition: To grasp the meaning, significance, or nature of something; to comprehend fully.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, understanding customer needs and market dynamics is crucial for developing effective strategies and products that resonate with target audiences.
vocabulary.nuance: Understanding often implies a deeper level of insight beyond surface knowledge, and it is essential for effective decision-making and relationship-building.

vocabulary.definition: The act of conveying information or expressing thoughts and feelings to others through verbal, non-verbal, or written means.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective communicating is vital in business for collaboration, negotiation, and maintaining relationships with clients, stakeholders, and team members.
vocabulary.nuance: Communicating encompasses not only the transmission of information but also the clarity and effectiveness of the message, which can greatly influence outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: To make strenuous or violent efforts to get free of restraint or resist attack; to experience difficulty or hardship.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business environment, struggle often refers to the challenges faced by individuals or teams in overcoming obstacles, achieving goals, or adapting to change.
vocabulary.nuance: Struggle can imply a sense of conflict or difficulty, and while it may indicate a negative experience, it can also lead to growth and resilience when addressed constructively.

text: The critique that is often leveled at Pets.com or at least at the time, was like, this is just a stupid business. They're shipping dog food around. You could never make that work, and that's just wrong. You absolutely can make it work.
speaker: Tom Conrad
context: Lenny discusses how Tom took Pets.com from nothing to a public company to completely out of business in 19 months. Tom defends the business model, noting that Chewy later proved online pet retail could work with a $9 billion valuation. Tom explains that timing was crucial - Pets.com launched when internet adoption was still very limited, making the logistics and customer acquisition much more challenging than it would be later.
text_ko: 당시 Pets.com에 대해 자주 나오던 비판은 “그건 그냥 말도 안 되는 사업이야. 개 사료를 배송한다고? 절대 성공할 수 없어”라는 식이었어요. 그런데 그건 틀렸어요. 충분히 성공시킬 수 있어요.
text_zh: 当时大家对Pets.com最大的质疑就是，这生意太蠢了，就是把狗粮快递来快递去的，这怎么可能赚钱嘛，但这种想法是错的。这个模式绝对是能跑通的。
text_es: La crítica que siempre le hacían a Pets.com, o al menos en ese momento, era algo como "este negocio no tiene sentido, están mandando comida para perros por todo el país, eso jamás va a funcionar", y eso está completamente equivocado. Claro que se puede hacer funcionar.
key_sentence: The critique that is often leveled at Pets.com was that it was a stupid business.
original_text: The critique that is often leveled at Pets.com or at least at the time, was like, this is just a stupid business. They're shipping dog food around. You could never make that work, and that's just wrong. You absolutely can make it work. Probably can't make it work when 80% of the country on the internet is still on dial up. It's really, really early.

vocabulary.definition: A detailed analysis and assessment of something, typically a literary, artistic, or academic work.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a critique often refers to feedback on a product, service, or strategy, helping organizations identify strengths and weaknesses.
vocabulary.nuance: While critiques can be constructive, they may also carry a negative connotation if perceived as overly harsh or dismissive.

text: For me, failure is not that you didn't drive revenue, failure is not learning. So it's really important that you learn when you fail.
speaker: Sri Batchu
context: Lenny asks Sri about creating a culture where people aren't afraid to take risks, given that growth experiments typically have only a 30% success rate. Sri explains his philosophy that the real failure isn't when experiments don't drive revenue - it's when teams don't learn from their failed attempts. He emphasizes the importance of designing conclusive tests to avoid repeatedly trying the same ineffective approaches.
text_ko: 제게 있어 실패는 수익(revenue)을 만들지 못한 게 아니라 거기서 배우지 못하는 거예요. 그래서 실패했을 땐 꼭 배우는 게 중요해요.
text_zh: 在我看来，失败不是因为你没有带来收入，真正的失败是没有从中学到东西。所以当你失败的时候，关键是要从中吸取教训。
text_es: Para mí, fracasar no es que no hayas generado ingresos, fracasar es no aprender nada. Por eso es súper importante que cuando las cosas no salen bien, saques algo en limpio.
original_text: For me, failure is not that you didn't drive revenue, failure is not learning. So it's really important that you learn when you fail. And so we celebrate failure as long as you're learning, and you can only learn if you've designed the right test and you failed conclusively, because otherwise I think many of us have been in situations where there's intuition that something might work and it doesn't work, and then you end up doing it over and over for years.

vocabulary.definition: Failure is the lack of success in achieving a desired outcome or goal, often resulting in setbacks or losses.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, failure is frequently viewed as a learning opportunity, encouraging teams to analyze mistakes and pivot strategies rather than simply focusing on negative results.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'failure' carries a negative connotation, in entrepreneurial contexts, it can also signify a crucial step towards eventual success and growth.

vocabulary.definition: Learning is the process of acquiring knowledge, skills, or understanding through experience, study, or instruction.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, continuous learning is essential for adapting to market changes, improving processes, and fostering innovation within teams.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'learning' emphasizes the importance of reflection and adaptation, particularly in contexts where mistakes have been made.

text: I think there wasn't really a clear path. I think there was [inaudible]. Exactly. And it was more just like if you understood, again, this is my point around unit economics, there are things where I think you have magical thinking around unit economics.
speaker: Jiaona Zhang (JZ)
context: Lenny asks JZ whether Airbnb Plus could have succeeded with better execution or if the business model was fundamentally flawed. Airbnb Plus was an attempt to create managed, inspected inventory to address trust issues, but it required significant operational investment. JZ explains that the project suffered from 'magical thinking' about unit economics - the belief that profitability would somehow emerge at scale without the fundamental economics working from the start.
text_ko: 사실 뚜렷한 길이 있었다고는 생각하지 않아요. (그 부분은 잘 안 들렸어요.) 맞아요. 그리고 다시 말하지만 제 요지는 유닛 이코노믹스(unit economics)에 관한 건데, 이 분야에 대해 마치 마법처럼 생각하는 경향이 있다고 봐요.
text_zh: 我觉得当时没有一个清晰的路径。我觉得有[听不清]。没错。更多的是，如果你理解的话，这又回到我说的单位经济效益(unit economics)的问题，有些事情你对单位经济效益(unit economics)抱有不切实际的幻想。
text_es: Creo que no había una ruta clara. Creo que había [inaudible]. Exacto. Y era más bien como que si entendías, otra vez, este es mi punto sobre la rentabilidad por unidad (unit economics), hay cosas donde creo que uno se hace ilusiones sobre la rentabilidad por unidad.
key_sentence: there are things where I think you have magical thinking around unit economics.
original_text: I think there wasn't really a clear path. I think there was [inaudible]. Exactly. And it was more just like if you understood, again, this is my point around unit economics, there are things where I think you have magical thinking around unit economics. You're like, 'Well, when we get to the scale of X, it's all going to work out. We can make these things happen.' I think you actually need to really make sure the unit economics work right at the beginning.

vocabulary.definition: Unit economics refers to the direct revenues and costs associated with a particular business model, typically expressed on a per-unit basis.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, understanding unit economics is crucial for assessing profitability and scalability, as it helps entrepreneurs determine how much profit or loss is generated from each unit sold.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a focus on the sustainability of a business model, and it is commonly used in discussions about financial health and growth potential.

vocabulary.definition: Magical thinking refers to the belief that one's thoughts, actions, or words can influence outcomes in a way that defies logic or rationality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, magical thinking can be critiqued when entrepreneurs or stakeholders hold unrealistic expectations about success without grounding their beliefs in data or practical analysis.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting naivety or a lack of critical thinking, and is best used to caution against overly optimistic or unfounded assumptions.

text: But between all of those highlights, there were so many B moments that get shoved under the rug because it's just easier for me and it's more impressive for others.
speaker: Gina Gotthilf
context: Lenny asks Gina about her concept of having both an 'A side' and 'B side' to everyone's career - where the A side contains impressive achievements that people share publicly. Gina explains that people naturally focus on sharing their highlights (A side) while hiding their failures and struggles (B side), but she believes it's important to acknowledge these B moments because they're a normal part of everyone's professional journey.
text_ko: 하지만 그 하이라이트들 사이사이에는 제게는 더 편하고 다른 사람들한테는 더 인상적으로 보이니까 그냥 묻혀버리는 B급 순간들(B moments)이 정말 많았어요.
text_zh: 但是在这些高光时刻之间，有太多平淡的B级时刻被我刻意掩盖了，因为这样对我来说更省事，对别人来说也更有面子。
text_es: Pero entre todos esos momentos de gloria, hubo muchas situaciones regulares que prefiero no mencionar porque me resulta más fácil y queda mejor con los demás.
key_sentence: Many B moments get shoved under the rug, but they are part of our lives.
original_text: But between all of those highlights, there were so many B moments that get shoved under the rug because it's just easier for me and it's more impressive for others. But I really like to highlight those because I think that most of us have a lot of B moments every day, every week, every month, and every period of our lives.

vocabulary.definition: Evoking admiration through size, quality, or skill; remarkable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, something that is impressive can refer to a product, presentation, or achievement that stands out and captures the attention of stakeholders or clients.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'impressive' generally has a positive connotation, it can sometimes imply that the quality is superficial or not backed by substance.

vocabulary.definition: The most important or notable parts of something; key features.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business report or presentation, highlights refer to the key achievements or significant data points that are emphasized to convey success or progress.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'highlights' suggests a focus on positive aspects, potentially overlooking less favorable details.

vocabulary.definition: To conceal or ignore something unpleasant or problematic.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate environment, issues that are 'shoved under the rug' may refer to unresolved conflicts or failures that are overlooked to maintain a facade of success.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase carries a negative connotation, suggesting avoidance rather than resolution, and is often used to criticize management practices.
